why: The matrix runner used to rebuild the binary on every invocation. A rebuild of identical source is not byte-reproducible, so a matrix run could never describe the same artifact as a cold-start run measured moments earlier, and the two records silently disagreed. The runner now accepts --reuse-binary, and this record was taken on the exact artifact measured by 2026-10-11-macos-release-terminal-gate.json.

sshMatrix.reconnectNote: Every reconnect case produced 11 unique session ids against 10 for the plain case, so each reconnect really tore the session down and built a new one rather than reusing the old channel.
sshMatrix.passwordFixtureFix: These two cases had been recorded as notRun because the fixture always ran `docker build`, which re-resolves debian:bookworm-slim and cannot complete while the Docker daemon is unable to reach the registry. The fixture now inspects for the local terminal-smoke-password-sshd image first and only builds when it is missing, and it settles on `exit` so a killed build cannot hang the runner. Both cases then passed on this same release binary.

limitations: Automated evidence only: no human physical keyboard, Chinese IME, Option/dead key or vim/nano coverage.
The localhost fixtures use generated keys and an ephemeral sshd; they do not stand in for the cross-platform real-machine matrix.
Windows OpenSSH Agent, Pageant, ConPTY/local Windows PTY and serial hardware remain unverified for lack of a test machine.
supersedes: the bef9cc8f measurement in this file's earlier revision
instrumentationCaveat: Smoke instrumentation (VITE_TERMINAL_SMOKE_BUILD=1) is required to run these cases, so this binary is not the shipping artifact. The cold-start record cites the same hash so both describe one build.
